**[SafeAI.watch](https://safeai.watch)** is a public record of AI safety and security for general readers: research, reported incidents, public warnings and policy responses. Each entry links its original source, gives its key points, and separates what happened from what the evidence shows.

The record holds 98 entries from Mar 22, 2023 to Oct 15, 2026 (27 warnings, 26 incidents, 25 governance, 20 research), drawn from 59 publishers. It is a selection, not a complete count: the burst above shows what the record covers, so its dense rim is no measure of how often such events happen. Read it on the site: [Latest](https://safeai.watch/latest), [Timeline](https://safeai.watch/timeline), [About](https://safeai.watch/about).

## How an entry reads

Every entry sets out what happened, the source's key points and what the evidence shows, and adds what remains uncertain when something material is still open. The newest one, from Oct 15, 2026, filed under Warnings:

> **Moderna co-founder Noubar Afeyan likens AI agents to living organisms and says sellers should have to prove them safe**
>
> **What happened.** At a Bloomberg New Economy Forum panel in New Delhi, Moderna co-founder and chairman Noubar Afeyan said AI agents are "crossing a threshold" and urged people to "think carefully about regulating agents that are being commercialized."
>
> **Key points.**
>
> - Afeyan said agents that adapt and act without human direction start to resemble "a living organism that has adapting capability, swarming capability, ecosystem building capability."
> - He said early 2026 warnings that agents would spread and form communities doing "unpredictable things" came true within six months, and that agents "can escape."
> - Citing thalidomide, he argued that those who sell agents should have to show they are safe; agents built for one's own use "may be harder to regulate."
> - He said unintended consequences such as new biomaterials also call for regulation: "Synthetic biology is another area which we really need to look at very carefully."
>
> **Evidence.** Recording of a panel discussion; one founder's argument, not evidence of harm. The automatic captions have no speaker labels, so attribution rests on the moderator's cues.
>
> **Source.** [Bloomberg Television · Video interview](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wJ434nBl19s)

## Run it locally

Needs Node.js 22.12.0 or later.

```bash
npm ci
npm run dev
```

The dev server runs at http://localhost:4321. `npm run build` writes the static site to `dist/`, and `npm run preview` serves that build. The build first runs `npm run film:lint`, which checks the About page film's script against its facts.

## Add or correct an entry

Entries live in [`src/data/events.json`](src/data/events.json). Each one has exactly these keys: `date` (the source's publication date, `YYYY-MM-DD`), `category` (one of `"Warnings"`, `"Incidents"`, `"Governance"`, `"Research"`), `title`, `happened`, `keyPoints` (a list of one to four short points), `evidence`, `source` (publisher and source type, such as "RAND · Research report") and `url` (https only), plus an optional `uncertain`. [`src/data/record.ts`](src/data/record.ts) checks every entry when the site builds and fails the build on a missing, empty or extra key, an empty or overlong `keyPoints` list, an unknown category, a date not written as `YYYY-MM-DD`, or a link that is not https. Run `npm run build` to check a change; CI runs the same build on every pull request.

The art above is generated from the same file. After changing the record, run `node scripts/readme/build.mjs` and commit `README.md` and `assets/readme/` with it; CI fails while they are out of date. Changes land through pull requests, and a merge to `main` deploys the site.

Spotted an error in an entry? [Open an issue](https://github.com/ryanportfolio/SafeAI.Watch/issues) with the entry's title and a source that shows the correction.

## What the project holds to

- Every entry links its original source.
- Each entry gives the source's key points and separates what happened from what the evidence shows, with what remains uncertain when something material is still open.
- No invented incidents, numbers or quotes. The site's illustrations are conceptual and carry no data; the chart at the top of this README is the exception, drawn from the record.
- No third-party trackers or analytics.

## Layout

| Path | Holds |
|---|---|
| `src/pages/` | The site's pages, built by [Astro](https://astro.build) as static HTML |
| `src/data/` | The record and its build-time checks |
| `src/scripts/visuals/` | The homepage's WebGL visuals |
| `src/scripts/film/`, `film/` | The About page film and its script |
| `scripts/film/` | The film's script check (`npm run film:lint`) and video export |
| `scripts/brand/` | The logo, icons and font subset (`npm run brand`) |
| `scripts/readme/` | This README and its art |
